name: International Public Partnerships Ltd
reason: Listed PPP/infrastructure investment fund whose reported EPS (GBP 0.17 in 2016, 0.04 in 2020) is fair-value movement on a discount-rate-sensitive portfolio, with 10y share count +7.9%/yr and 10y avg ROE 6.1%; a yield vehicle with no route to 7% per-share growth.

name: Banco Comercial Portugues S.A.
reason: Portuguese turnaround bank with 10y avg ROE 6.3%, EPS EUR 0.06 (2015) collapsing to 0.01-0.02 through 2016-22 and only recovering to 0.07 on the rate tailwind, shares +13%/yr over 10y and Polish CHF-mortgage/Mozambique exposure; fails the US through-cycle bank standard.

name: Catena AB
reason: Swedish logistics property owner whose FFO/share rose SEK 10.2 (2016) to 25.6 (2025) only with shares +8.9%/yr and net debt/EBITDA 8.2x, margin at its 10y high (80.9%) and consensus growth of 2.3%/6.6%/2.4% for FY1-FY3; growth is equity- and debt-funded, not a 7% organic route.

name: Johnson Matthey Plc
reason: Adjusted EPS fell from GBP 2.39 (2018) to 1.34 (2025) with EBIT margin of 2.6% and 10y ROIC 6.6%; core Clean Air autocatalyst profits face the credible 5-yr EV threat and PGM Services earnings are set by metal prices.

name: Linea Directa Aseguradora SA
reason: Spanish direct motor/home insurer with high ROE (10y avg 24%) but EPS EUR 0.10 (2017) to 0.08 (2025) after a 2023 loss from claims inflation; underwriting-cycle earner with no growth record and a mature domestic motor market.

name: KBC Ancora SCA
reason: Single-asset holding company of KBC Group shares whose EPS (EUR 4.09-5.06 in 2025-26 vs -0.27 in 2016) is simply pass-through KBC dividends set by the bank's rate/credit cycle and payout policy; no business of its own, express via KBC if wanted.

name: EFG International AG
reason: Swiss private bank with EPS CHF 0.24 (2016) to 1.03 (2025) and consensus +11.5%/+19.9% but 10y avg ROE 9.6%, shares +7.3%/yr (BSI deal) and earnings tied to AUM/transaction fees and rates, i.e. capital-markets activity, matching US wealth-manager precedent.

name: AL Sydbank A/S
reason: Danish regional bank whose EPS fell DKK 21.16 (2016) to 13.10 (2020) through the zero-rate years before peaking at 57.86 (2023) on NIM, consensus FY1 -2.3%, and the 2025 three-way AL Sydbank merger is a transformational deal; not a through-cycle best-in-class bank.

name: Lumo Homes Plc
reason: Finnish residential landlord (ex-Kojamo) with FFO/share EUR 0.68 (2023) falling to 0.57 (2025), net debt/EBITDA 11.7x, 10y ROIC 4.5% and a Helsinki rental oversupply; no growth route and a heavily levered balance sheet.

name: Legal & General Group Plc
reason: UK annuity/PRT insurer and asset manager with adjusted EPS GBP 0.22 (2016) to 0.21 (2025) (10y CAGR 1.3%), a 174% average adjusted-vs-GAAP gap and consensus FY2 +2.4%; earnings depend on rates, credit spreads and bulk annuity pricing with no 7% route.

name: Persimmon Plc
reason: UK housebuilder with EPS GBP 2.84 (2018) to 1.00 (2025) and EBIT margin from 28.8% to 10.9%; earnings are set by the housing/mortgage-rate cycle and planning policy, matching the US homebuilder precedent.

name: Sparebanken Norge
reason: Norwegian savings bank (Sparebanken Vest/Sor merger) with EPS NOK 9.04 (2021) to 16.56 (2025) on the rate cycle, share count +16.5%/yr from the merger, and consensus FY1 -3.9% then ~5%/yr; growth well below 7% at peak NIM.

name: SPAREBANK 1 SOR-NORGE ASA
reason: Decent Norwegian savings bank (EPS NOK 6.58 in 2016 to 11.75 in 2021 through low rates, 10y avg ROE 11.8%) but EPS of 16.98 is a peak-NIM high, 2020 EPS fell 49% on oil-region credit losses, and the Oct-2024 SR-Bank/Sorlandet merger plus consensus 0%/9.5%/5.8% leave the path unforecastable.

name: Erste Bank Polska S.A.
reason: Polish bank whose EPS fell from PLN 22.33 (2017) to 10.88 (2021) through the zero-rate years before tripling to 63.24 (2025) on NIM, with consensus FY1 -20%, CHF-mortgage litigation and bank-tax policy risk and a 2025 change of control from Santander to Erste.

name: Land Securities Group PLC
reason: UK office/retail REIT with EPRA EPS GBP 0.49 (FY2016) to 0.52 (FY2025) (10y CAGR 1.2%), 10y avg ROE -1.9%, net debt/EBITDA 10.3x and EBIT margin at its 9th percentile; structural office/retail headwinds and consensus 0-7%.

name: Sirius Real Estate Limited
reason: German/UK business-park landlord whose FFO/share rose EUR 0.034 to 0.088 largely via acquisitions (acq/FCF 0.39) and equity issuance (shares +7.2%/yr), with net debt/EBITDA 7.2x and consensus FY2-FY3 of +4.8%/+3.1%; levered, acquisition-led growth.

name: B&M European Value Retail PLC
reason: UK discount variety retailer with a real value proposition but EPS halved from GBP 0.43 (FY2020) to 0.21 (FY2025), EBIT margin down from 13.1% to 7.6% (18th pctile), lease-adjusted net debt/EBITDA 2.9x and consensus FY1 +2.2%; competitive erosion and the turnaround cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: HICL Infrastructure PLC
reason: Listed PPP/regulated-infrastructure fund with EPS GBP 0.12 (2016) to 0.14 (2025) driven by fair-value/discount-rate moves, 10y avg ROE 6.0% and shares +3.9%/yr; a concession-runoff yield vehicle with no route to 7% growth.

name: Construcciones y Auxiliar de Ferrocarriles S.A.
reason: Spanish rolling-stock maker whose EPS (EUR 4.27 in 2025, a 10y high) swings with lumpy public tenders (2020 -64%), with EBIT margin of 5.0% and 10y avg ROIC 4.3%; low-return contract manufacturing with no moat.

name: BRD Groupe Societe Generale SA (Romania)
reason: Romanian SocGen-controlled bank with high ROE (10y avg 16.5%) but EPS RON 2.06 (2018) to only 2.22 (2025), consensus FY1 -2.4% and a doubled Romanian bank turnover tax; earnings set by the rate cycle and fiscal policy with no 7% route.
